name: Meal Planner
description: The family's meals for the week, day by day (Breakfast, Lunch and Dinner), with a shared grocery list and the family's recipe book; not for school runs, chores or appointments.

for: The family's meals for the week: Breakfast, Lunch and Dinner, day by day
A shared grocery list grouped by aisle
The family's own recipe book, with a recipe's ingredients added to the list
Planning the week's dishes from the recipe book
notFor: School runs, chores or appointments (use checklist or tracker)
Ordering groceries from a store: a connector does that
A restaurant's menu or a business kitchen

agentInterface.instructions: Meal Planner owns this family's meals, recipes, shopping list, drafts, orders, pantry stock and shopping preferences. Never keep any of it in memory or chat: read the app before you answer, change it only through its operations, then tell the family what the app now says. Read the guide operation before shopping, answering a job or changing meals. A meal is a set of recipes plus a note: when plans change, change the recipes and note (set_meal_recipes, save_meal), not just the dish text. Only you add recipes, and only after searching for the same dish under another spelling. Nothing in the app runs until it knows the household: when the family tells you who eats, their food habits, which meals to plan and where they shop, save it in their words as the household.profile setting (PATCH /a/<this app>/api/_app/settings); never fill it from guesses or the app's own rows. Background jobs (review_meal, fill_recipe, find_patterns) and background facts (shelf life, recipe lines) are your informed guesses: never ask the family about them and never message anyone for them. The app sends the reminders and menus itself; message the family only when a Shopping timeline wake asks (the price step), then ack_message; or when they talk to you. Silence means carry on. Never order without a family member's explicit yes; record it (record_yes), place the order, then record_order at once.
